names: 22nd Street Caltrain Station ADA Access Improvement
distance_note: The existing 22nd St Caltrain station (Pennsylvania Ave/Indiana St, Dogpatch) sits roughly 400-450m from both Pier 70's and Potrero Power Station's tracked boundaries -- grouped here under Pier 70 as the closer, better-established Dogpatch association.
summary: An accessibility retrofit of the existing, below-grade 22nd Street Caltrain station -- the only regular-service Caltrain station without wheelchair access. The project adds ramps to both platforms plus wayfinding and safety improvements. The design phase is funded and scheduled, not shown as started: the SFCTA Board approved $1.3 million for it in April 2026 and Caltrain expects to complete design by summer 2027. Sources disagree on when the station would open for use: June 2029 (SFCTA's April 2026 post and presentation), December 2029 (the project description in SFCTA's April 14 packet) and "the end of 2029" (The Voice of San Francisco, October 2026), all subject to funding. In September 2026 the Federal Transit Administration announced a $14.1 million All Stations Accessibility Program award to Caltrain's board for the station (Trains.com, September 16, 2026). Sponsored by the Peninsula Corridor Joint Powers Board (Caltrain) with SFCTA (Prop L) and FTA funding.

milestones.text: Caltrain and SFCTA were applying for federal grant funding for the station's accessibility project, seeking about $9 million from the Federal Transit Administration (Green Caltrain, February 4, 2024: "are applying for federal grant funding"; "seeking $9 million"). The month is the date of that report; the source does not say when the effort began, and it refers to a 2021 study that came before.

SFCTA's Transportation Authority Board packet for its April 14, 2026 meeting recommends $1,300,000 in Prop L funds for the project's design phase, part of a total funding plan of $19,134,000 (Planning/Conceptual Engineering $734,000 already spent via Prop K; Design Engineering $1,300,000 via Prop L; Construction $17,100,000, an engineer's estimate at 30% design). The Board approved the allocation at that meeting (SFCTA, April 28, 2026: "During the April 14 Transportation Authority Board meeting, board members approved $9.8 million in Prop L sales tax funds").

SFCTA Board gives final approval to the $1,300,000 Prop L design-phase allocation, first approved on April 14 (one of three projects sharing a combined $9.8M Prop L allocation, alongside the Powell St Improvement and the Mission Bay Ferry Landing). SFCTA's April 28 post: "The Transportation Authority Board gave final approval at the April 28 meeting."

The Federal Transit Administration announces an All Stations Accessibility Program award of $14.1 million to the Peninsula Corridor Joint Powers Board for ADA improvements at the 22nd Street station (an announced date, not a grant agreement or construction start): Trains.com, published September 16, 2026, says the agency announced the awards "last week". Railway Supply (September 12, 2026) says the FTA published its selection list on September 10 and Progressive Railroading is dated September 11; the FTA's own announcement was not read. The amount is close to the funding gap SFCTA's April 2026 plan had left as "Planned TBD".
Design (PS&E, Plans/Specifications/Estimate) targeted complete; Caltrain expects to complete the design phase by summer 2027 (SFCTA, April 28, 2026).

Expected, not scheduled: the project is expected to open for use in 2029, subject to funding. The month differs by source: June 2029 (SFCTA's April 28, 2026 post, "seeking construction funding to implement the project by June 2029", and the April 14 presentation, "Open for use expected June 2029"), December 2029 (SFCTA's April 14 packet, project description: "have the project open for use by December 2029, subject to funding availability"; its allocation form lists "Open for Use" in April-June 2029) and "project completion by the end of 2029" (The Voice of San Francisco, October 6, 2026). Construction was not yet funded in April 2026; the FTA announced a $14.1 million award in September 2026, but no source gives a construction schedule.

costs.what: Total project cost per SFCTA's April 2026 funding plan (Planning/Conceptual Engineering $734,000 already spent via Prop K; Design Engineering $1,300,000 via Prop L; Construction $17,100,000, an engineer's estimate at 30% design); SFCTA's April 14, 2026 board packet, allocation request form: "Funding Plan for Entire Project Total: $16,147,000 [planned] $2,253,000 [programmed] $734,000 [allocated] $19,134,000". An estimate at 30% design, not a contract amount
Prop L design-phase allocation, approved by the SFCTA Board on April 14, 2026 and given final approval on April 28 (SFCTA, April 28, 2026)

Federal Transit Administration All Stations Accessibility Program award announced for this project's ADA improvements (Peninsula Corridor Joint Powers Board); the announcement was in September 2026 (Trains.com, September 16: "last week"), and no grant agreement was read

facts.value: Peninsula Corridor Joint Powers Board (Caltrain), with funding from SFCTA (Prop L) and the FTA

One ramp on the northbound platform (about 305 ft long, 6.5% slope) and one on the southbound platform (about 465 ft long, 6.1% slope), plus tactile strips, lighting and signage. Platforms sit about 25 ft below street grade, currently reachable only by stairs.

open_questions: This record's placement under Pier 70 rather than Potrero Power Station reflects a roughly equal real-world distance (about 400-450m to each tracked boundary) plus the station's more established association with the Dogpatch/Pier 70 corridor in transit planning -- not a precise geometry test against a real station footprint (no Assessor parcel or site-plan figure exists to test against; the map shape is a coarse placeholder box; see its accuracy note).

No source says design work has begun or how far along it is. SFCTA's April 14, 2026 packet schedules design from April 2026 to September 2027 ("Review 30% design and other documentation: 7/1/26 – 8/1/26"; geotechnical report "anticipated October 2026") and gives "Start Construction" as April-June 2028, but that is a plan written before the work, and no source dated after the planned start reports progress.

When the station would open for use is given three ways: June 2029 (SFCTA's April 28, 2026 post and its April 14 presentation), December 2029 (the project description in SFCTA's April 14 packet) and the end of 2029 (The Voice of San Francisco, October 6, 2026). The packet's own allocation form lists "Open for Use" in April-June 2029 and "Project Completion (means last eligible expenditure)" in July-September 2029. All are subject to funding, which was not secured when the dates were written; the record shows 2029 only.
